options.C: A tool for measuring vocabulary size.
options.D: A method to calculate reading speed.

questions.explanation: The grammatical rank scale is a hierarchical ordering of linguistic units, from the smallest to the largest.

questions.stem: The text suggests that the purposes of formal listening, such as comprehending, criticizing, and evaluating, are:

options.A: Completely separate and never occur together.
options.C: Not mutually exclusive and may occur during a single lecture.

questions.explanation: You may have to engage in listening for multiple purposes at once, like comprehending, criticizing, and evaluating a concept or theory during one lecture.

questions.stem: What is the term for the process of combining words to create new ones, like 'copycat'?
questions.explanation: Word formation includes compounding (combining words).

questions.stem: Biographies and autobiographies can be classified under ________ essay.
questions.explanation: A narrative essay tells a story or recounts events chronologically. Because biographies and autobiographies recount the sequence of an individual's life, they fall under narrative writing.

questions.stem: What is an acronym?

options.A: A word formed by clipping the end of another word.
options.B: A word formed from the initial letters of other words and pronounced as a word.
options.C: A word borrowed from another language.
options.D: A word whose class has changed without adding an affix.

questions.explanation: Word formation processes include acronymy, forming a word from initial letters and pronouncing it as a word.

questions.stem: For some reason, I .................... a change in her attitude
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Perceived'.

questions.stem: Which grammatical unit consists of a group of words without a subject or predicate?
questions.explanation: A phrase is a group of words without a subject or a predicate, but functions as a component of a sentence.

questions.stem: Words relating to measurement, location, size, and colour are helper words for which type of paragraph?
questions.explanation: The Descriptive Paragraph uses helper words relating to measurement, location, size, length, colour, etc., to describe a person, place, or thing.

questions.stem: What is the core element of a noun phrase?
questions.explanation: In a noun phrase (MHQ), the headword (H) is the core noun.

questions.stem: The colon is used in the following situations except

options.A: to introduce direct speeches in some contexts
options.B: to introduce the name of the publisher in a text
options.C: to introduce a list as part of a sentence
options.D: to break a title into two parts

questions.explanation: The colon is not used to introduce the name of the publisher in a text; this is not a standard colon usage.

questions.stem: What function does a noun clause serve when it answers 'who' or 'what' receives the action of a verb?
questions.explanation: A noun clause functions as the Object of a Verb when it answers who or what receives the action.

questions.stem: is referred to as the meat of the essay.
questions.explanation: In the COEM evaluation framework for essay writing, Content provides the actual substance, ideas, and arguments-the 'meat' of the essay.

questions.stem: What kind of clause is introduced by relative pronouns like 'who', 'which', or 'that'?
questions.explanation: An adjectival/relative clause is usually introduced by relative pronouns.

questions.stem: Ranking of articles retrieved from databases is by ...........

options.C: No of times the search was conducted

questions.explanation: Database search results are typically ranked, or sorted, by criteria such as date (newest first) or relevance to the search query.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an Adverbial Clause of Condition?

options.A: I will go if it stops raining.
options.B: I left because I was tired.
options.C: He runs as if he is flying.
options.D: I will wait until you arrive.

questions.explanation: Adverbial Clauses of Condition express a condition and use words like 'if' or 'unless'.

questions.stem: ........ is the punctuation mark used to express all forms of excitement.
questions.explanation: The exclamation mark is used to express strong emotions or excitement.

questions.stem: How many main clauses are in a simple sentence?
questions.explanation: A simple sentence consists of exactly one main clause that expresses a complete thought.

questions.stem: The "period" is also written as _________ in punctuation
questions.explanation: The period is also commonly referred to as a full stop, especially in British English.

questions.stem: Which sentence type gives a command or makes a request?
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence is a statement that gives command, request or directives.

questions.stem: All of these are examples of transitional words or phrases except one. Which one is it?
questions.explanation: 'In addition' (additive), 'as a result' (causal), and 'by the same token' (comparative) are all standard transitional phrases. 'Of course' is more of an interjection or a comment, not a typical transition to link ideas.

questions.stem: What is one way to ensure you do not take on more than is necessary?
questions.explanation: Time management requires you to never take on more than is necessary; learn to say no.

questions.stem: The name of an author whose idea is cited in research writing must appear in.......
questions.explanation: All sources cited within the text of a research paper must have full details listed in the reference list (or bibliography) at the end.

questions.stem: Why is it important to employ a program of physical and mental fitness?

options.A: It looks good on a resume.
options.B: It helps maintain the energy and focus needed for proper time management.
options.C: It reduces the amount of time you have to study.
options.D: It is required by the university.

questions.explanation: Employing a program of physical and mental fitness is a key tip for managing yourself and your time effectively.

questions.stem: Apostrophes are used
questions.explanation: Apostrophes are used to signify possession or contractions (omitted letters, e.g., don't, it's).

questions.stem: What is meant by 'managing your backlog'?

options.B: Creating more tasks for the future.
options.C: Clearing out accumulated pending tasks so they do not disrupt your current schedule.

questions.explanation: Manage backlog to ensure that pending tasks do not overwhelm your current and future time schedules.

questions.stem: What is the function of support or detail sentences in a paragraph?

options.B: To provide the evidence and analysis that makes the claim digestible.
options.C: To transition to the next paragraph.

questions.explanation: Support or Detail Sentences provide the evidence/analysis that makes your claim digestible.

questions.stem: Which of these is a helpful psychological solution for time management?

options.A: Always seek perfection in every minor task.

questions.explanation: Psychological solutions to time management problems include having self-discipline.

questions.stem: A good paragraph, like a good composition, should exhibit what two qualities?
questions.explanation: A good paragraph would exhibit unity and coherence just like a good composition would exhibit the same quality amongst paragraphs.

questions.stem: How can you deal with an overwhelming project?

options.A: Break it down into smaller tasks with manageable steps.
options.C: Do it all the night before it is due.
options.D: Ask the lecturer to cancel it.

questions.explanation: Breakdown your goals into smaller tasks with manageable steps.

questions.stem: Why should you check the publication date of a book during the survey step?

options.A: To know how old the book is for a collection.
options.B: To see if the material in the publication is current or not.
options.C: To determine the price of the book.
options.D: To find out the author's age.

questions.explanation: It is important to check the publication date to see if the material in the publication is current or not.

questions.stem: What role does punctuality play in time management?

options.B: It shows respect for your own time and others' time.
options.D: It reduces your overall study time.

questions.explanation: Being punctual is a core tip for successful time management.

questions.stem: Why is improving our capacity for informal listening important?

options.B: To improve our relationships with others.
options.C: To become a better public speaker.
options.D: To get a job after graduation.

questions.explanation: While not for passing exams, improving informal listening is essential to improve our relationships with the people we interact with daily.

questions.stem: Why should you NOT hurry up to do things faster?

options.A: Hurrying up is not always the best way of doing a thing faster because it leads to errors.
options.B: Because it takes too much energy.
options.C: Because it makes you look unprofessional.
options.D: Because time slows down when you hurry.

questions.explanation: Hurrying up is not always the best way of doing a thing faster, as it can compromise quality and cause mistakes.

questions.stem: To be elected ................, candidates must have a solid background in law enforcement.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Sheriff'.

questions.stem: What should you do instead of 'thinking about unnecessary things'?

options.A: Become a busybody in other people's matters.
options.B: Focus on your set targets and avoid distractions.

questions.explanation: Never think about unnecessary things and never be a busybody in other people's matters.

questions.stem: Which of these sentences has a plural compound subject?

options.A: The man and his wife were present.
options.B: Waiter is the rice and beans ready?
options.C: The MD and Chief Executive Officer of the company was introduced
options.D: Hot lemonade and honey is good for a cold.

questions.explanation: In option A, 'The man and his wife' is a compound subject joined by 'and', which takes a plural verb ('were'). The other options have singular compound subjects referring to the same thing or a single dish.

questions.stem: What does it mean to 'operate within your strengths'?

options.B: Analyze yourself and perform tasks in ways that utilize your best skills and peak energy times.
options.D: Force yourself to do things you hate.

questions.explanation: Analyze yourself and operate within your strengths to maximize efficiency.

questions.stem: /s/, /t/, and /n/ are related based on their what of articulation?
questions.explanation: The sounds /s/, /t/, and /n/ are all alveolar sounds. This means they are all produced with the tongue touching or near the alveolar ridge, the bony ridge just behind the upper teeth. Therefore, they are related by their place of articulation.

questions.stem: Which is an example of setting a goal in clear terms?

options.A: I will do better this semester.
options.C: I will get up at 4:30am to revise for one hour every day.

questions.explanation: Set your targets in clear terms. Don't write 'I want to study more'; rather 'Get up at 4.30am to revise for one hour every day'.

questions.stem: An ellipsis is a series of what?
questions.explanation: An ellipsis is a punctuation mark consisting of three periods (or dots) in a row, used to indicate an omission or a pause.

questions.stem: Why is it advised to use time-saving devices like ATMs and mobile banking?

options.B: They help maximize your use of time by reducing physical visits to banks.
options.D: They eliminate the need for a timetable.

questions.explanation: Time saving devices can help maximise your use of time: taking a taxi, using ATMs or mobile banking.

questions.stem: What is the ability to locate, retrieve, and evaluate information known as?
questions.explanation: Information literacy is the set of skills that includes identifying an information need, and then effectively and ethically locating, retrieving, evaluating, and using that information.

questions.stem: How should a student approach 'free time' in a time table?

options.B: Allow for enough flexibility for un-programmed but necessary activities.
options.D: Use it entirely for social media.

questions.explanation: It should be adaptable... allow for enough flexibility for un-programmed but necessary activities.

questions.stem: When writing a summary, what should you do if you get stuck?

options.C: Copy a sentence from the original.
options.D: Stop writing and repeat the step of reading to pick out essentials.

questions.explanation: If you get stuck, stop writing and repeat step 2, which is reading to pick out the essentials.

questions.stem: What is the consequence of postponement?

options.B: It leads to a backlog of tasks and a bad habit.

questions.explanation: Postponement of planned events is an avoidable bad habit that ruins time management.

questions.stem: Why should you avoid hasty generalizations and conclusions while listening to a lecture?

options.A: Because you might be wrong and the lecturer will penalize you.
options.B: To ensure you can leave the lecture early.
options.C: Because there might still be something in the speaker's message you will benefit from.

questions.explanation: Even if parts of the delivery are agitating or irritating, it is possible that there is still valuable information to be gained, so you should listen to the end.

questions.stem: What does the statement 'Time is life, do not waste it' imply?

options.B: Proper time management is essential to a fulfilling and successful life.

questions.explanation: Treat each day as your last, maximize it, because time is life.

questions.stem: In note-taking shorthand, what does 'NB' stand for?
questions.explanation: 'NB' is an abbreviation for 'note well', used to draw attention to an important point.

questions.stem: How does digital literacy empower students?

options.A: It makes them forget traditional literacy.
options.B: It allows them to participate productively in the digital economy and study effectively.
options.C: It forces them to stay online 24/7.
options.D: It teaches them how to build computers.

questions.explanation: Students must develop different types of literacy that can help them to study effectively, behave responsibly online and participate productively in the digital economy.

questions.stem: What is the function of the word "boy" in the sentence: That boy is my cousin?
questions.explanation: In the sentence, 'boy' is the subject of the verb 'is'.

questions.stem: Which of these is a key difference between Web 1.0 and Web 2.0?

options.A: Web 1.0 was interactive; Web 2.0 is static.
options.B: Web 2.0 allows users to be active creators of content, rather than just passive consumers.
options.D: Web 2.0 does not use the internet.

questions.explanation: The emergence of Web 2.0 technologies shifted users from being passive consumers to becoming active creators of digital content.

questions.stem: The acronym LEARNER is associated with which type of reading?
questions.explanation: To achieve productive study reading, you need to follow the acronym LEARNER.

questions.stem: Why is evaluating information critical in the 21st century?

options.A: Because all information online is true.
options.B: Due to the overwhelming abundance of information, including misinformation and disinformation.
options.C: Because printed books are no longer published.

questions.explanation: Because of the sheer volume of information available, critical evaluation is necessary to spot misinformation and disinformation.

questions.stem: A pollutant is any substance that is present in a quantity that:

options.B: Changes the color of the environment
options.C: Causes harm to resident organisms or disrupts ecological balance

questions.explanation: A pollutant is any substance present in a quantity or concentration that causes harm to resident organisms or disrupts the ecological balance.

questions.stem: What is 'phishing'?

options.B: A cyber attack designed to trick individuals into revealing sensitive personal information.
options.C: A method for searching library databases.
options.D: A tool for evaluating text similarity.

questions.explanation: Protect dimension involves ensuring privacy... and avoiding phishing scams.

questions.stem: The text suggests that one way to identify the function and purpose of a lecture for note-taking is to:

options.B: Begin an overview of the lecture's outline as you listen.

questions.explanation: You can identify potentially important information by doing an overview of the outline of the lecture or text simultaneously as you listen or read.

questions.stem: When assessing the 'Purpose' of a source using the CRAAP test, what are you looking for?

options.A: The spelling errors in the text.
options.B: Whether the motive behind publishing the source was to inform, teach, sell, entertain, or persuade.
options.C: How recently the article was published.

questions.explanation: Purpose: What was the motive behind publishing the source? (To inform, teach, sell, entertain, or persuade?).

questions.stem: A question mark is not used at the end of ............
questions.explanation: An indirect question (e.g., 'He asked where I was going') is a statement and ends with a period, not a question mark.

questions.stem: What is the primary danger of using an informal email address like 'babygirl4life@yahoo.com' for academic purposes?

options.B: Lecturers and future employers may judge the student negatively for lacking a professional digital identity.

questions.explanation: Lecturers and future employers judge students by their digital identities, so using informal ones is risky.

questions.stem: What is the general term for an association between members of the same or different species?
questions.explanation: Symbiosis is a broad term that simply means an association between members of the same or different species.

questions.stem: How can a student ethically use AI tools?

options.A: By copying and pasting AI output directly into assignments.
options.B: By using AI to write exams.
options.C: By verifying outputs, avoiding plagiarism, and protecting personal data.
options.D: By refusing to cite the use of AI.

questions.explanation: Students must learn to use AI tools ethically by verifying outputs, avoiding plagiarism, and protecting personal data.

questions.stem: A/an _____ paragraph describes a series of events or a process in some sort of order.
questions.explanation: A sequence paragraph organizes information in a specific order, often chronological, to describe events or a process.

questions.stem: What is 'algorithmic power' in the context of AI?

options.A: The electricity required to run a computer.
options.B: The ability of AI systems to make decisions that influence human behavior and opportunities.
options.C: The speed of an internet connection.
options.D: The battery life of a smartphone.

questions.explanation: Critical AI literacy involves understanding algorithmic power and ethics.

questions.stem: An example of a specialized dictionary is
questions.explanation: Oxford and Webster are general dictionaries. A specialized dictionary focuses on a specific subject or register, such as a dictionary of slang or a glossary of medical terms.

questions.stem: Why might an AI system produce biased suggestions?

options.B: Due to limitations and biases in its training data.
options.C: Because the AI dislikes certain users.

questions.explanation: AI systems can misinterpret cultural context or produce biased suggestions due to limitations in training data.

questions.stem: The sentence: They lost some extremely valuable documents in the fire. The expression: extremely valuable is an example of a[No] - _____
questions.explanation: 'Extremely valuable' functions as an adjective phrase, modifying the noun 'documents'.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a question you should ask when evaluating an AI tool?

options.A: What biases may be present in the system?
options.B: Whose knowledge or culture is privileged or excluded?
options.C: How can I use this to avoid studying completely?
options.D: What data was used to train this system?

questions.explanation: Critical questions include asking about biases, data training, and privileged cultures, not how to avoid studying.

questions.stem: Skimming involves the following except

options.C: looking at the table of contents

questions.explanation: Looking for very specific details or facts is the definition of scanning. Skimming is broader and involves surveying the abstract, table of contents, and blurbs.

questions.stem: What does 'Currency' refer to in the CRAAP test?

options.A: The cost of accessing the information.
options.B: Whether the source is up to date and when it was published.
options.C: The monetary value of the website.
options.D: The language the text is written in.

questions.explanation: Currency: Is the source up to date? When was the information published or posted?.

questions.stem: One of the following skills is not necessary in note-taking.
questions.explanation: Note-taking involves skills like summarizing, paraphrasing, and reducing sentences. Sound articulation is related to speech production, not note-taking.

questions.stem: What constitutes 'digital writing' today?

options.A: Using a smart pen on physical paper.
options.B: Entering information into online forms, writing blog posts, and sending emails.

questions.explanation: Writing in the 21st century also includes digital writing: entering information into online forms, creating professional profiles, writing blog posts, etc.

questions.stem: How many pure vowels or monophthongs are there in English?
questions.explanation: There are twenty vowel sounds in English. Twelve of them are pure vowels or monophthongs.

questions.stem: In the context of literacies, what is the meaning of being a 'meaning maker'?

options.B: Comprehending the text at the level intended by the author.
options.C: Rewriting the text to change its meaning.
options.D: Only looking at the pictures in a text.

questions.explanation: Meaning maker: Comprehending the text at the level intended by the author.

questions.stem: Listening to comprehend or gain a general understanding of the lecture is ________ listening.
questions.explanation: Listening in an academic setting with the goal of comprehension is characterized as formal listening.

questions.stem: What does a 'text critic' understand about texts?

options.A: That all texts are perfectly neutral.
options.B: That existing biases inform calls to action and that texts are not neutral.
options.C: That texts should only be read once.
options.D: That grammar is the only important aspect of reading.

questions.explanation: Text critic: Understanding that the text is not neutral, and that existing biases inform calls to action.

questions.stem: To achieve depth in the treatment of a topic, the writer is advised to ......
questions.explanation: To achieve depth, the writer should limit or narrow the subject.

questions.stem: What is an effective way to stay mentally active during a lecture?

options.B: Take effective notes by interacting with the information and making decisions about what to record.
options.C: Record the lecture on a phone and go to sleep.

questions.explanation: Taking effective notes requires a student to be mentally active... interact with information, make decisions about what to record, and write.

questions.stem: One of the following is not a linking device:
questions.explanation: 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction, not primarily a linking device for connecting equal ideas.

questions.stem: Why is listening considered a 'purposeful activity'?

options.A: Because you have no choice but to do it.
options.B: Because a listener is on the lookout for something in particular, requiring focus and effort.
options.C: Because it happens automatically without thinking.
options.D: Because it is exactly the same as hearing.

questions.explanation: A listener is on the lookout for something in particular. In other words, listening is a purposeful activity.

questions.stem: The ability to recognize when information is needed is called .........
questions.explanation: Information literacy is the set of skills that includes the ability to recognize when information is needed.

questions.stem: What physiological factor could reduce the effectiveness of listening?
questions.explanation: Physical factors include hunger, illness, hearing defect.

questions.stem: What is the recommended approach to writing what the lecturer is saying?

options.B: Use 'shorthand' with symbols and abbreviations instead of writing verbatim.
options.C: Record the lecture and write it all out later.
options.D: Only write down what is written on the board.

questions.explanation: You should not attempt to write verbatim. Instead, you should learn to use 'shorthand' through symbols, abbreviations, and concept maps.

questions.stem: Which of these is a psychological factor that hinders listening?

options.B: Dislike or disrespect for the lecturer.

questions.explanation: Psychological factors include mental fatigue, a wrong mental attitude, dislike/disrespect for the lecturer.

questions.stem: When a book is written by more than six authors, a researcher using the APA referencing style should ________ when citing in the reference list

options.A: Not list any other names after the sixth author but write et al. in their place
options.C: Write the names of the first six authors
options.D: Provide the name of the first three authors

questions.explanation: According to the specific APA format guidelines taught in this GST module, works with more than six authors require listing the first six, followed by ellipses or 'et al.' to indicate the remaining authors.

questions.stem: When a lecturer uses the phrase 'let me give you an example', what is the signpost function?
questions.explanation: Exemplifying signpost words include 'to illustrate this', 'for example', 'let me give you an example'.

questions.stem: A quote is used in research write up to..................
questions.explanation: Quotations are used in research to support arguments and provide evidence from authoritative sources.

questions.stem: What does the signpost word 'finally' indicate?

options.A: The lecturer is introducing a new topic.
options.B: The lecturer is summarising or ending a list.
options.C: The lecturer is giving an example.

questions.explanation: Summarising words like 'finally', 'in short', 'to sum up' mean the speaker is moving to a conclusion.

questions.stem: Which of the following consonants does NOT occur in the onset position of an English syllable?
questions.explanation: While /ŋ/ and /ʒ/ do not occur in the onset position.

questions.stem: Which type of diagram is best for showing the chronology of a continuous process?
questions.explanation: Cycle diagrams show processes, relationships, and the chronology of a continuous cycle.

questions.stem: _____ is not a bilabial sound.
questions.explanation: /f/ is a labiodental sound, produced with the lower lip and upper teeth. /m/, /b/, and /p/ are bilabial sounds produced with both lips.

questions.stem: What are Radial Diagrams (or webs) useful for?

options.B: Displaying facts, aspects, attributes, or examples of a particular topic.

questions.explanation: Radial diagrams (also called 'webs') are helpful in displaying facts, and aspects, attributes, or examples of a particular topic.

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of consonants permissible at the beginning of an English syllable?
questions.explanation: English syllable structure allows for a maximum of three consonants in the onset, or beginning, of a syllable, as in the word 'splash' /splæʃ/.

questions.stem: Why is 'Charting' an effective note-taking method?

options.B: It allows information to be recorded in a table with columns and headings for easy comparison.
options.D: It is a completely linear format.

questions.explanation: In Charting, information is recorded in a table format with columns and headings.

questions.stem: The element which makes a paragraph easily understandable to the reader is....
questions.explanation: Coherence is the quality that makes a paragraph easily understandable by ensuring ideas flow smoothly and logically.

questions.stem: What is a major disadvantage of a bound notebook for note-taking?

options.B: It is secure but not very flexible for adding or reorganizing notes.

questions.explanation: Notebook - secure and easy to carry, but not very flexible in use.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of highlighting key points while reading?

options.A: To make the book look used.
options.B: To locate main ideas easily and remember where to find information for later revision.
options.C: To slow down your reading speed.
options.D: To impress others with your study habits.

questions.explanation: In order to locate the main ideas easily and remember where to find certain pieces of information in the material, you need to read with a highlighter or a pen in hand.

questions.stem: What does it mean to be an 'active listener'?

options.B: Being fully involved in the listening process and interacting with the material.

questions.explanation: Active listening describes the process of being fully involved, which includes taking notes and evaluating the material.

questions.stem: Declarative sentences end with a/an
questions.explanation: A declarative sentence makes a statement or expresses an opinion and ends with a period (full stop).

questions.stem: What is the purpose of 'Informational Listening'?

options.B: To evaluate the validity of an argument.
options.D: To enjoy the sound of the speaker's voice.

questions.explanation: Whenever you listen to learn something, you are engaged in informational listening.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrectly spelled word below
questions.explanation: 'Souvenier' is misspelled; the correct spelling is 'souvenir'.

questions.stem: Why is it advised to review your notes immediately after a lecture?

options.A: Because the lecturer will collect them.
options.B: To fill in gaps while the information is still fresh and prevent the rapid 50% memory loss.
options.C: To memorize them word for word.
options.D: To throw them away if they are messy.

questions.explanation: Because we forget 50% within an hour, post-listening activities like reviewing and summarizing are crucial.

questions.stem: Internal citation appears in the body of manuscript
questions.explanation: Internal citation (in-text citation) appears in the body of the manuscript.

questions.stem: What does non-verbal communication from a lecturer (like gesturing or changing tone) often indicate?

options.B: They are signaling an important point or structural shift in the lecture.
options.C: They want the class to leave.

questions.explanation: Movements, gestures, or pauses signal to the attentive listener to be on the lookout for an important point.

questions.stem: What can be consulted for instruction on how to do things?
questions.explanation: A manual, also known as a handbook or instruction guide, is specifically designed to provide instructions or guidance on how to perform a task or operate something.

questions.stem: Which of these sounds is an example of an English plosive?
questions.explanation: Plosives include /p, b, t, d, k, g/

questions.stem: Repeating key words or using pronouns to refer to nouns in previous sentences are examples of:
questions.explanation: Verbal bridges include repeating key words and using pronouns to link ideas.

questions.stem: Which of these sounds is an English affricate?
questions.explanation: English affricates are /tʃ/ and /dʒ/

questions.stem: The man jogs regularly.
questions.explanation: 'Regularly' indicates how often the action occurs, making it an adverb of frequency.

questions.stem: What characterizes the Place of Articulation for 'Velar' sounds?

options.B: The tongue tip touches the alveolar ridge.
options.C: The back of the tongue rises to the soft palate.

questions.explanation: Velar: The back of the tongue rises to the soft palate (e.g., /k, g, ŋ/).

questions.stem: In the context of formal listening, what does listening 'to learn' enable a student to do?

options.A: Memorize facts for a single exam.
options.B: Outline, account for, and discuss the historical development of an event or theory.
options.C: Ignore the historical context of a subject.

questions.explanation: Listening to learn enables a student to be able to outline, account for, and discuss the historical development of an event, a theory, a concept, etc.

questions.stem: Which part of the vocal tract is completely blocked during the production of nasal sounds?
questions.explanation: Nasals: The oral cavity is blocked, but the velum is lowered so air escapes through the nose.

questions.stem: How can you turn the title 'The Causes of Election Violence' into a question for previewing?

options.A: Is election violence caused by voters?
options.B: What are the causes of election violence?

questions.explanation: You could rephrase the title to form a question, e.g., 'The Causes of Election Violence' can be turned into 'What are the causes of election violence?'

questions.stem: What is the distinction between 'voiced' and 'voiceless' consonants based on?

options.B: Whether the vocal folds vibrate or not.
options.C: Whether air escapes through the nose.
options.D: Whether the sound is loud or soft.

questions.explanation: If the vocal folds are held together and vibrate... the sound is voiced. If they are held apart and do not vibrate, the sound is voiceless.

questions.stem: The part of a word to which other elements can be added is called_____
questions.explanation: A root or stem is the core part of a word to which prefixes and suffixes (other elements) can be added.

questions.stem: Which of these pairs represents a voiceless/voiced pair of bilabial plosives?
questions.explanation: /p/ is voiceless and /b/ is voiced; both are bilabial plosives.

questions.stem: What is commensalism?

options.B: One species benefits, the other is harmed
options.C: One species benefits, the other is not affected

questions.explanation: In commensalism, one species (the commensal) benefits, while the other (the host) is neither benefited nor harmed.

questions.stem: How do vowels differ fundamentally from consonants?

options.B: Vowels involve a continuous flow of air with little or no obstruction in the vocal tract.
options.C: Vowels are only produced in the nasal cavity.

questions.explanation: Unlike consonants, vowels involve a continuous flow of air with little or no obstruction in the vocal tract.

questions.stem: What is more important for a student to retain understanding for a longer previous time?
questions.explanation: Reviewing notes after a lecture is a key strategy for transferring information to long-term memory and retaining understanding.

questions.stem: What are the three main criteria used to classify vowels?

options.B: Tongue Height, Tongue Part (Advancement), and Lip Position.

questions.explanation: Vowels are classified primarily by: Tongue Height, Tongue Part, and Lip Position.

questions.stem: Avoiding premature conclusions allows the listener to grasp the ________ meaning of the lecture.
questions.explanation: By not jumping to conclusions early, a listener can understand the full and intended meaning presented by the speaker.

questions.stem: What does it mean if a vowel is classified as a 'Front' vowel?

options.B: The front of the tongue is raised towards the hard palate.
options.C: The back of the tongue is raised.

questions.explanation: Front: The front of the tongue is raised towards the hard palate.

questions.stem: One can search the library catalogue for information materials using all these EXCEPT.......
questions.explanation: Library catalogues can typically be searched by author, title, and subject. Language is usually a filter, not a primary search field.

questions.stem: What is the phonetic symbol for the long vowel sound in 'car'?
questions.explanation: The long vowel /ɑː/ is used in words like 'car' and 'father'.

questions.stem: ________ , according to experts, produces the strongest effect on stress placement than all the other features.
questions.explanation: While loudness, length, and vowel quality contribute to stress, experts agree that pitch (change in tone or musical note) is the most powerful perceptual cue for identifying a stressed syllable in English.

questions.stem: What defines a 'Closing diphthong'?

options.A: It glides towards the central vowel /ə/.
options.C: It glides towards a higher vowel (/ɪ/ or /ʊ/).
options.D: It requires the mouth to close completely.

questions.explanation: Closing diphthongs: glide towards a higher vowel (/ɪ/ or /ʊ/).

questions.stem: is the use of the pitch of the voice to convey meaning or syntactic information.
questions.explanation: Intonation is formally defined as the melodic rise and fall of voice pitch used to convey attitudinal or syntactic (grammatical) meaning.

questions.stem: Which diphthong is present in the word 'boy'?
questions.explanation: The word 'boy' contains the closing diphthong /ɔɪ/.

questions.stem: What is the chief aim of a narrative essay?

options.A: To prove a point with logic.
options.B: To analyze a phenomenon in detail.
options.C: To arouse and sustain interest, making the reader feel a good story has been told.

questions.explanation: The chief aim of the narrative essay is to arouse and sustain interest; to make the reader feel that a good story has been told.

questions.stem: Why is English intonation important?

options.A: It makes the speaker sound musical.
options.B: It helps convey grammatical meaning, emotion, and attitude, distinguishing a statement from a question.
options.C: It dictates how words are spelled.

questions.explanation: Intonation helps convey grammatical meaning (e.g., making a statement vs. asking a question) and shows the speaker's emotion.

questions.stem: The text mentions that after a lecture, you should try out a summary of the lecture:
questions.explanation: After the lecture, you should 'try out a summary of the lecture in his/her own words'.

questions.stem: What substitution might a Nigerian English speaker make for the voiceless dental fricative /θ/ (as in 'think')?
questions.explanation: Southern Nigerian speakers often substitute them with alveolar plosives ([t] for /θ/).

questions.stem: A finite clause contains one of the following
questions.explanation: A finite clause contains a verb that changes for tense, person, and number.

questions.stem: Which conjunction connects a dependent clause to an independent clause?
questions.explanation: Subordinating conjunctions link dependent and independent clauses.

questions.stem: Which articulators are described as relatively fixed and do not move to articulate with other organs?
questions.explanation: Passive articulators are the relatively fixed organs, such as the teeth and hard palate, that do not move.

questions.stem: Which interjection is commonly used to express disgust?
questions.explanation: Ew (or Yuck) expresses disgust.

questions.stem: Features which apply to units higher than the segments are known as
questions.explanation: Features like stress and intonation that stretch over whole syllables, words, or sentences (units above individual consonant/vowel segments) are classified as suprasegmentals.

questions.stem: Which interjection expresses relief?
questions.explanation: Phew expresses relief or exhaustion.

questions.stem: Which criterion for predicting stress involves considering the number of syllables in a word and their internal constitution?
questions.explanation: The phonological criterion involves a consideration of the phonological structure of the word, i.e., considering the number of syllables and their internal constitution.

questions.stem: Which article is used before a singular, countable noun mentioned for the first time?
questions.explanation: Indefinite articles are used for first-time or general mentions.

questions.stem: Interjections are usually punctuated with a[No]
questions.explanation: Interjections expressing sudden or strong emotion are punctuated with the exclamation mark.

questions.stem: Which article is used before the word 'hour'?
questions.explanation: 'Hour' starts with a silent 'h' and a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.stem: When intonation aids turn-taking, it performs a/an _____ function.
questions.explanation: When intonation helps manage conversation flow, such as signaling when it's someone's turn to speak, it is performing a discourse function.

questions.stem: Which article is used before plural nouns in a general sense (e.g., 'Apples are good for you')?
questions.explanation: The zero article is used for generic plural nouns.

questions.stem: The vowel /u:/ is produced with which kind of lip rounding?
questions.explanation: The lips may be rounded, as in /ɒ/, /ʊ/, /ɔ:/, and /u:/.

questions.stem: In 'She likes both tea and coffee', what type of conjunction is 'both... and'?
questions.explanation: Correlative conjunctions work in pairs.

questions.stem: Students are advised to maintain ________ contact with their lecturers during classes.
questions.explanation: Maintaining eye contact is a key non-verbal cue in active listening. It helps the student stay focused and shows the lecturer they are engaged.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a clause from a phrase?

options.A: A phrase has a subject and a verb; a clause does not.
options.B: A clause has a subject and a verb; a phrase does not.
options.C: A phrase is longer than a clause.
options.D: A clause can never stand alone.

questions.explanation: A clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb, unlike a phrase which lacks them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a criterion for predicting stress?
questions.explanation: Stress placement in words can often be predicted based on morphological (word structure), phonological (sound patterns), and syntactic (grammatical function) criteria. Semantic meaning, on its own, is not a primary criterion for predicting stress.

questions.stem: What are the components of the 'MHQ' noun phrase structure?
questions.explanation: The structure of a noun phrase is MHQ, wherein M- modifier, H - head, and Q- qualifier.

questions.stem: The final step in writing a paragraph summary is to:

options.B: Compare your summary with the original and make necessary revisions.

questions.explanation: The final step is to compare this digested form with the original for accuracy and to make whatever revisions this comparison suggests.

questions.stem: What does a Prepositional Phrase consist of?
questions.explanation: Prepositional Phrase (PP) - consists of a preposition and its object.

questions.stem: In English Is one of the best ways to acquire new words.
questions.explanation: Reading widely provides the greatest volume of exposure to diverse, contextualized vocabulary, accelerating vocabulary development.

questions.stem: What is the function of a Noun Clause acting as the 'Subject of a Verb'?

options.B: It tells what the sentence is about.
options.C: It answers who receives the action.

questions.explanation: Subject of a Verb: When it functions as the subject, it basically tells what the sentence is about.

questions.stem: My mother cooks very well.
questions.explanation: 'Very well' describes how she cooks, indicating the manner of the action.

questions.stem: What function does an Adjectival Clause perform?

options.C: It modifies a noun or a pronoun.

questions.explanation: An adjectival/relative clause functions as an adjective, it qualifies a noun or a pronoun.

questions.stem: What punctuation mark is used to introduce a list?
questions.explanation: A colon (:) is the punctuation mark used to introduce a list, a quotation, or an explanation that follows an independent clause.

questions.stem: Which Adverbial Clause answers the question 'how?'
questions.explanation: Adverbial Clauses of Manner answer the question 'how?'.

questions.stem: In the sentence: 'They came late because of the heavy rain', the phrase the heavy rain is called?
questions.explanation: 'The heavy rain' is a group of words centered around the head noun 'rain,' which is modified by the article 'the' and the adjective 'heavy.' Therefore, it is a noun phrase.

questions.stem: Which sentence structure contains two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction?
questions.explanation: A compound sentence contains two or more main clauses linked together by coordinating conjunctions.

questions.stem: is a receptive skill.
questions.explanation: Both reading and listening are formally taught as receptive communication skills, where information is absorbed. Speaking and writing are productive skills.

questions.stem: What is an independent (main) clause?

options.A: A clause that cannot stand alone.
options.B: A clause that acts as an adjective.
options.C: A clause that can stand on its own and convey complete meaning.
options.D: A clause that has no subject.

questions.explanation: A main or independent clause can stand on its own and convey complete meaning.

questions.stem: What kind of essay emphasizes character and setting?
questions.explanation: A narrative essay tells a story. A key part of storytelling is the development of characters and the description of the setting where the events take place.

questions.stem: What is the function of a Declarative sentence?

options.D: To give a piece of information in a statement form.

questions.explanation: A declarative sentence gives a piece of information in a statement form and ends with a full stop.

questions.stem: Information can be in form of ................
questions.explanation: Information can be presented in various forms, including numbers, texts, and graphs & charts, so 'All' is the correct answer.

questions.stem: What type of question is 'Where did you put the keys?'
questions.explanation: Wh- Questions use question words like where, why, who, etc.

questions.stem: In English ……. Is one of the best ways to acquire new words.
questions.explanation: Reading widely is one of the best ways to acquire new vocabulary.

questions.stem: What type of question is 'They arrived early, didn’t they?'
questions.explanation: Tag Questions consist of a statement followed by a mini-question (tag) like 'didn't they?'.

questions.stem: When a word is long word is shortened to make it less awkward for speech, it is referred to as a.........
questions.explanation: The process of shortening a long word without changing its meaning is called clipping (e.g., 'ad' from 'advertisement').

questions.stem: Which sentence is an Imperative sentence?
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command, request or directive.

questions.stem: The acronym 'OPAC' means
questions.explanation: OPAC stands for Online Public Access Catalogue, the computerized database of materials held in a library.

questions.stem: Which sentence is an Exclamatory sentence?
questions.explanation: An exclamatory sentence expresses feelings or opinion in an emphatic way and ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.stem: Vowel distinctions do not include:
questions.explanation: Vowels are classified as monophthongs (single sound), diphthongs (two sounds), and triphthongs (three sounds). 'Quadriphthongs' is not a recognized category in phonetics.

questions.stem: What is 'clipping' in word formation?

options.D: Changing a noun to a verb.

questions.explanation: Clipping is shortening a word, e.g., 'phone' from 'telephone'.

questions.stem: The thesis statement is to an essay what the ______ is to a paragraph.
questions.explanation: The thesis statement presents the main argument or focus of an entire essay, while the topic sentence presents the main idea of a single paragraph. They serve analogous roles at different structural levels.

questions.stem: What is 'borrowing' in word formation?
questions.explanation: Borrowing involves adopting words from other languages into English.

questions.stem: Wow! Oh no! and Watch it! Are ___________
questions.explanation: 'Wow!', 'Oh no!', and 'Watch it!' are examples of interjections, which are words or phrases used to express strong emotion or surprise.

questions.stem: What is a 'verb phrase'?

options.C: The main verb and its auxiliaries.

questions.explanation: A verb phrase (VP) includes the main verb and its auxiliaries.

questions.stem: ________ is the ability of the listener to receive, perceive and decode the meaning of what the lecturer is disseminating.
questions.explanation: Listening is explicitly defined as the receptive ability to receive, perceive, and decode spoken messages.

questions.stem: What does it mean to set your targets in 'clear terms'?

options.B: Being specific, like stating exact times and durations for tasks.
options.C: Only sharing your goals with friends.
options.D: Writing your goals in a different language.

questions.explanation: Setting targets in clear terms means being specific. Don't write 'I want to study more'; rather 'Get up at 4.30am to revise for one hour'.

questions.stem: The prominence of one syllable over other syllables in a word is a function of _____
questions.explanation: The linguistic term for the overall prominence of one syllable over others in a word is 'stress'.

questions.stem: How can forming study groups help with time management?

options.A: It gives you an excuse to socialize.
options.B: It allows for task sharing so each student does fewer activities.
options.C: It makes the lecturer like you more.
options.D: It eliminates the need for exams.

questions.explanation: Students can form study groups and share the tasks so each student does fewer activities.

questions.stem: What function do topic sentences serve when read in sequence throughout an essay?

options.A: They provide a list of all examples used.
options.B: They provide a sketch of the essay's argument.

questions.explanation: When read in sequence, an essay's topic sentences provide a sketch of the essay's argument.

questions.stem: Why should a student evaluate their present achievement data?

options.A: To set target goals for personal improvement.
options.C: To decide whether to drop out.
options.D: To avoid studying in the future.

questions.explanation: Goal setting involves using your present achievement data to set target goals for personal improvement.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of sentences advised for a paragraph?
questions.explanation: You are advised to write a minimum of three sentences in a paragraph.

questions.stem: What happens when a student fails to manage their backlog?

options.B: Pending tasks overwhelm their current and future time schedules.
options.D: Lecturers give them higher grades out of pity.

questions.explanation: Manage backlog to ensure that pending tasks do not overwhelm your current and future time schedules.

questions.stem: .............. is consulted mostly by speech makers and writers
questions.explanation: A Book of Quotations is consulted mostly by speech makers and writers.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a 'schedule or planner'?

options.A: To carry around as a fashion accessory.
options.B: To chart the way ahead and get organized.

questions.explanation: Employ a schedule or planner/calendar to chart the way ahead and get organized.

questions.stem: Note-taking complements
questions.explanation: The curriculum explicitly ties effective note-taking to active listening. Note-taking complements and reinforces what is absorbed through listening during a lecture.

questions.stem: Why should a student 'never cease striving to become more efficient'?

options.A: Because time management is an ongoing process of improvement.
options.B: Because efficiency is the only thing that matters in life.
options.C: So they can eventually stop working entirely.

questions.explanation: Never cease striving to become more efficient and effective; time management requires continuous optimization.

questions.stem: The goal of an argumentative essay is to.........
questions.explanation: The goal of an argumentative essay is to persuade the audience, convince the readers, and sell an idea, so 'all of the above' is correct.

questions.stem: What does giving up a movie to attend tutorials illustrate?

options.B: Making a sacrifice to begin working towards achieving a set goal.

questions.explanation: Begin to work towards achieving your goals, for example: Give up movies to attend tutorials.

questions.stem: A word usually has _____ primarily-stressed syllable(s).
questions.explanation: In English phonology, no matter how long a word is, it generally only has one single syllable that carries the primary stress (the peak of prominence).

questions.stem: Why is it crucial to evaluate the 'Currency' of a digital source?

options.A: To see how much money the author makes.
options.B: To ensure the information is up-to-date and not obsolete.
options.D: To find out what country it was written in.

questions.explanation: Currency asks: Is the source up to date? When was the information published or posted?

questions.stem: Referencing is composed of which two parts?
questions.explanation: A complete reference or citation typically consists of two parts: an in-text citation (brief note within the body of the paper) and a corresponding full reference list entry at the end of the paper.

questions.stem: In the CRAAP test, what does 'Relevance' determine?

options.B: If the source actually meets the specific needs of your research or assignment.

questions.explanation: Relevance asks: Is the source relevant to your research?

questions.stem: A/an ________ paragraph describes a series of events or a process in some sort of order.
questions.explanation: A sequence paragraph is specifically structured to describe a series of events or a process ordered chronologically or logically.

questions.stem: What is a major risk of relying solely on ChatGPT for academic research?

options.B: It might hallucinate and provide fabricated references that look real.
options.C: It uses too much internet data.

questions.explanation: AI can 'hallucinate' and generate plausible-looking references that do not exist in real journals.

questions.stem: When a word is long word is shortened to make it less awkward for speech, it is referred to as a………
questions.explanation: The process of shortening a long word without changing its meaning is called clipping (e.g., 'ad' from 'advertisement').

questions.stem: How should a student interact with an AI-generated essay draft?

options.B: By verifying the outputs and checking for biases or inaccuracies before use.
options.C: By claiming they wrote every word themselves.
options.D: By deleting it and using a typewriter.

questions.explanation: A critically AI-literate student must verify AI outputs, avoid plagiarism, and check for biases.

questions.stem: One of these is not a minor sentence
questions.explanation: Gatekeeper wanted is a complete sentence with an implied subject; the others are minor sentences without full clause structure.

questions.stem: What describes the transition from Web 1.0 to Web 2.0?

options.A: Moving from color to black-and-white screens.
options.B: Moving from reading static web pages to actively creating and sharing content.
options.C: Moving from laptops to desktop computers.
options.D: Moving from fast to slow internet speeds.

questions.explanation: The emergence of Web 2.0 technologies shifted users from being passive consumers to becoming active creators of digital content.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a lentic freshwater habitat?
questions.explanation: Lentic habitats are standing or still water bodies, such as ponds and lakes.

questions.stem: What role does 'cybersecurity' play in digital literacy?

options.A: It is a way to hack other students' grades.
options.B: It is part of the 'Protect' dimension, keeping personal data safe from phishing.
options.C: It is only for computer science majors.
options.D: It allows you to download movies illegally.

questions.explanation: The Protect dimension involves ensuring privacy, cybersecurity, and avoiding phishing scams.

questions.stem: Which criterion for predicting stress involves a consideration of the internal structure of English words, such as whether they are simple, compound, or complex?
questions.explanation: The morphological criterion involves a consideration of the morphological or internal structure of English words.

questions.stem: Why must an individual's digital identity be managed carefully?

options.A: Because you can only have one password.
options.B: Because it forms a permanent digital footprint evaluated by future employers and lecturers.
options.C: Because the government bans informal emails.
options.D: Because it takes up storage space on your phone.

questions.explanation: Lecturers and future employers judge students by their digital identities, making careful management critical.

questions.stem: _____ is used to introduce a list
questions.explanation: The colon is the specific punctuation mark employed to introduce a list of items.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of reflecting on 'problem areas' after a lecture?

options.B: To identify difficult technical words and seek help early.
options.C: To find reasons to drop the course.

questions.explanation: Reflect on problem areas such as difficult technical words and concepts, and seek help early.

questions.stem: The text suggests that you should arrive for the lecture in time to sit where you can:

options.A: Be near the door to leave early.
options.B: Have close contact with the lecturer.
options.D: Be in the back of the room.

questions.explanation: One of the pre-lecture activities is to arrive on time to sit where you can have close contact with the lecturer, presumably to see and hear better.

questions.stem: Why is a 'wrong mental attitude' detrimental to listening?

options.B: It is a psychological factor that blocks the objective reception of information.
options.C: It makes the room feel colder.
options.D: It drains the battery of your recording device.

questions.explanation: Psychological factors include a wrong mental attitude, which reduces the effectiveness of purposeful listening.

questions.stem: What is the immediate goal of argumentative or persuasive writing?

options.B: To sell an idea or convince readers to make up or change their minds.

questions.explanation: The immediate goal of this type of writing is to sell an idea or convince readers to either make up or change their minds on an issue.

questions.stem: How do signpost words like 'firstly, secondly, lastly' help a listener?

options.A: They show the speaker is lost.
options.B: They indicate the lecturer is listing points in a specific order.
options.C: They mean the class is over.
options.D: They show the speaker is angry.

questions.explanation: Listing signpost words like 'firstly', 'secondly' show the direction and order of the speaker's thoughts.

questions.stem: What does 'unity' in a paragraph refer to?

options.B: The paragraph concerning itself with a single focus.
options.C: The use of many different ideas.

questions.explanation: Unity means the entire paragraph should concern itself with a single focus.

questions.stem: What does a 'target diagram' visually represent?

options.B: The relationships between or among two or more classes using circles to show membership.

questions.explanation: Target diagrams express the relationships between or among two or more classes, using circles to show membership.

questions.stem: According to the text, reading is also a process of what?
questions.explanation: Reading is also a process of communication by which essentially, most formal activities of learning take place.

questions.stem: Why is 'mental fatigue' classified as a psychological factor rather than a physical one?

options.A: Because it only happens at night.
options.B: Because it originates from the mind of the listener and affects cognitive focus.
options.D: Because it affects the ears directly.

questions.explanation: Psychological factors which come from the mind include mental fatigue, anxiety, and emotional trauma.

questions.stem: A biography is

options.A: A detailed description of a person's life written by someone else
options.D: An account of a person's life written by himself or herself

questions.explanation: A biography is an account of an individual's life written by a different person. (If written by the person themselves, it is an autobiography).

questions.stem: What makes 'charting' distinct from 'outlining' in note-taking?

options.B: Charting uses a table format with columns and headings for comparisons.
options.D: Charting is done before the lecture begins.

questions.explanation: In Charting, information is recorded in a table format with columns and headings.

questions.stem: What is the benefit of using 'filing cards' for notes?

options.A: They hold lots of long paragraphs.
options.B: They are good for headings and very useful during revision.

questions.explanation: Filing cards - good for headings, very useful in revision.

questions.stem: When is an offence of self-plagiarism said to have been committed?

options.A: You copy from the internet without acknowledgement
options.B: You copy from your lecturer's handout without acknowledgement
options.D: You copy from your previous assignment for a new assignment without acknowledgment

questions.explanation: Self-plagiarism occurs when a student or researcher reuses their own previously submitted work or data for a new assignment or publication without properly citing or acknowledging the prior use.

questions.stem: Why should a student discuss what they have learnt with classmates after a lecture?

options.B: It serves as a post-listening activity to reinforce memory and understanding.

questions.explanation: Post-listening activities: After the lecture, discuss what you have learnt with your classmates.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a mark of a serious student?

options.A: reading at a specific time and place

questions.explanation: A serious student typically plans their reading (time, place, timetable) and avoids distractions. Reading study materials anywhere may not always be conducive to effective study.

questions.stem: What makes the English vowel /ɜː/ difficult for Nigerian speakers?

options.B: It doesn't exist in many indigenous languages, leading to substitutions like /ɔː/ or /a/.
options.C: It requires closing the mouth completely.
options.D: It is only spoken by Americans.

questions.explanation: Because /ɜː/ does not exist in most Nigerian indigenous languages, many speakers substitute it with /ɔː/ or /a/.

questions.stem: Conjunctive adverbs function in a sentence to

options.A: magnify the relationship between clauses of concurrent status in a sentence
options.B: these clarify the relationship between clauses of concurrent status in a sentence
options.C: clarify the relationship between clauses of unequal status in a sentence
options.D: clarify the relationship between clauses of equal status in a sentence

questions.explanation: Conjunctive adverbs clarify the relationship between clauses of equal status in a sentence.

questions.stem: What is the defining physical characteristic of a 'bilabial' sound?

options.A: It is produced using the teeth and tongue.
options.B: It is produced using both lips coming together.
options.C: It requires the velum to be raised.

questions.explanation: Bilabial sounds are produced when both lips come together (e.g., /p, b, m, w/).

questions.stem: .......are allowed access into Gandhi Library
questions.explanation: Access to Gandhi Library, which houses special collections like Africana, is typically restricted to researchers and postgraduate students.

questions.stem: How does a 'triphthong' differ from a 'diphthong'?

options.A: It involves a continuous glide through three vowel qualities without a break.
options.C: It is only used in writing.
options.D: It takes three times as long to say.

questions.explanation: A triphthong is a glide from one vowel sound to another, and then to a third, all produced smoothly without any break.

questions.stem: Quotation marks are used to indicate:

options.B: A third party statement or direct speech.
options.C: The title of your own essay.

questions.explanation: Quotation marks are used to indicate that what is being written is a third party statement (direct speech).

questions.stem: What does the 'stress-timed' nature of English mean for unstressed syllables?

options.B: They are often shortened or squashed together to fit the regular rhythm.
options.C: They are stretched out to take up more time.

questions.explanation: In a stress-timed rhythm, stressed syllables appear at regular intervals, and unstressed syllables are squashed together.

questions.stem: Publications issued in successive parts, at regular intervals, and intended to be continued indefinitely are .......
questions.explanation: Publications issued successively at regular intervals indefinitely are serials collection.

questions.stem: Why do some non-native speakers produce an 'in-elastic timed' rhythm in English?

options.B: Due to the non-reduction of weak vowels, giving every syllable equal duration.
options.C: Because they pause after every word.
options.D: Because they use too much intonation.

questions.explanation: Non-reduction of vowels means every syllable demands equal attention, creating an 'in-elastic timed' rhythm.

questions.stem: Affixes which cause stress to move from one syllable to another are known as _____ affixes.
questions.explanation: Affixes that cause the stress to shift from one syllable to another in the base word are called stress-moving affixes.

questions.stem: What does 'pulmonic egressive' mean regarding airflow in speech?

options.A: Air is pulled into the nose.
options.B: Air is pushed out from the lungs to create sound.

questions.explanation: Pulmonic egressive means the air stream is pushed out from the lungs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an activity to engage in before a lecture to enhance comprehension and note-taking?

options.B: Revising previous lectures that relate to the current one.

questions.explanation: Revising previous lectures, reading about the topic, and checking new words are all activities recommended to be done before the lecture.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an alveolar sound?
questions.explanation: Alveolar sounds occur when the tongue tip or blade touches the alveolar ridge (e.g., /t, d, s, z/).

questions.stem: APA recommends that a book without an author should be cited in the text using

options.D: The first few words of the title, year of publication and page number

questions.explanation: When a source lacks an author, APA style dictates using a shortened version of the title in the in-text citation in place of the author's name, along with the year and page number if needed.

questions.stem: What is the definition of a 'bound morpheme'?

options.B: It can stand alone as a word.
options.C: It cannot stand alone and must attach to a free morpheme to convey meaning.
options.D: It is a type of conjunction.

questions.explanation: A bound morpheme cannot stand alone but will have to be attached to a free morpheme to express full meaning.

questions.stem: Which clause patterns is reflected in this sentence: Kofi became the president.
questions.explanation: The sentence 'Kofi became the president' follows the Subject + Verb + Complement (SVC) pattern, where the complement ('the president') describes or identifies the subject.

questions.stem: What differentiates a 'proper noun' from a 'common noun'?

options.A: A proper noun refers to a specific, unique entity and is usually capitalized.
options.B: A proper noun is always plural.
options.C: A proper noun represents abstract ideas.
options.D: A proper noun is a verb in disguise.

questions.explanation: A proper noun refers to a specific person, location, or thing (e.g., Ademola, Atlantic Ocean).

questions.stem: A three consonant onset obligatorily has ________ as the first consonant.
questions.explanation: A three-consonant onset obligatorily has /s/ as the first consonant.

questions.stem: How do 'inflectional morphemes' affect verbs?

options.B: They indicate tense, such as adding '-ed' for past tense, without changing the core meaning.
options.C: They remove the verb from the sentence.

questions.explanation: Inflectional affixes do not change meaning or class but indicate tense, number, or degree.

questions.stem: Why is moving the head from side to side while reading considered a deficiency?

options.A: It helps to focus on the text.
options.B: It prevents the eyes from totally focusing and slows down reading.
options.C: It is a sign of good concentration.

questions.explanation: Moving the head from side to side prevents the eyes from totally focusing on what is being read and the mind follows the movement, dividing attention and slowing speed.

questions.stem: What is the role of 'demonstrative pronouns'?

options.C: To point to specific things relative to the speaker, like this, that, these, those.

questions.explanation: Demonstrative pronouns point to specific nouns (this, that, these, those).

questions.stem: Two models of spelling popular in English are …….. and
questions.explanation: The two dominant orthographic standards recognized and taught in the English language are British spelling and American spelling.

questions.stem: Why are 'be, have, and do' called primary auxiliary verbs?

options.B: They can function as both helping verbs and main lexical verbs.
options.C: They are only used in the past tense.
options.D: They are completely optional in a sentence.

questions.explanation: The primary auxiliary verbs are 'be', 'have', and 'do', which can also act as main verbs.

questions.stem: Referencing style is determined by.
questions.explanation: Different academic disciplines demand different referencing styles. For example, Social Sciences typically use APA, while the Humanities use MLA.

questions.stem: What characterizes an 'intransitive verb'?

options.C: It does not require a direct object to complete its meaning.
options.D: It only exists in the present tense.

questions.explanation: Intransitive verbs do not require an object (e.g., She sleeps).

questions.stem: An Explanation Paragraph is concerned with:

options.C: Explaining how or why something happens.

questions.explanation: The Explanation Paragraph explains how or why something happens, exploring causes and effects.

questions.stem: In what situation is the 'passive voice' often preferred?

options.A: When you want a forceful, direct sentence.
options.B: When the performer of the action is unknown or less important than the action itself.

questions.explanation: Passive voice can be useful when the performer of the action is unknown or unimportant.

questions.stem: What does reading provide the opportunity to garner?
questions.explanation: Reading provides you the opportunity to garner information necessary for growth.

questions.stem: What do 'correlative conjunctions' always do?

options.B: Stand alone as a complete sentence.
options.C: Work in pairs to connect grammatically equal elements.

questions.explanation: Correlative conjunctions work in pairs to connect grammatically similar elements (e.g., either/or).

questions.stem: In the LEARNER acronym for study reading, what does the 'R' stand for?

options.A: Read all materials on the topic.

questions.explanation: In the LEARNER acronym: R - Read all materials on the topic to find answers to set out questions.

questions.stem: How do 'adverbs of degree' modify other words?

options.A: By showing when an action happened.
options.B: By expressing the intensity or extent of an action or quality, like 'extremely'.
options.C: By stating where the action took place.

questions.explanation: Adverbs of Degree show the intensity or extent of something (e.g., very, too, extremely).

questions.stem: Combination of letters and figures indicating the classes of a book in a library is known as.........
questions.explanation: The combination of letters and figures that indicates a book's classification and location on the shelf is known as a call mark or call number.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a 'preposition of manner' from a 'preposition of place'?

options.A: A preposition of manner explains how something is done, rather than where.
options.B: A preposition of manner uses numbers.
options.C: A preposition of manner acts as a verb.
options.D: A preposition of manner only applies to time.

questions.explanation: Manner prepositions explain how or why something happens, unlike place prepositions which indicate location.

questions.stem: What does 'pre-reading' involve?

options.B: Reading the preliminary details like the introductory paragraph and conclusion before the actual reading.

questions.explanation: Pre-reading involves reading the preliminary details like the introductory paragraph before the actual reading, and often the conclusion as well.

questions.stem: Why are 'interjections' considered grammatically independent?

options.A: Because they are banned from formal writing.
options.B: Because they do not alter or connect to the grammatical structure of the main sentence.
options.C: Because they are always single letters.
options.D: Because they replace the subject of the sentence.

questions.explanation: Interjections are grammatically independent of the rest of the sentence.

questions.stem: Which group of diphthongs has a first element that is either a mid or low vowel and a high vowel second element?
questions.explanation: Closing or Rising diphthongs have a first element that is either a mid or low vowel and a high vowel second element.

questions.stem: When should the 'zero article' be applied to an uncountable noun?

options.B: When discussing it in a general, non-specific sense.
options.C: When the noun starts with a vowel.
options.D: When it is the last word in a sentence.

questions.explanation: The zero article is used with generic nouns when talking about plural or uncountable nouns in a general sense.

questions.stem: What does SQ3R refer to?
questions.explanation: SQ3R is a well-known reading comprehension method. The acronym stands for Survey, Question, Read, Recite, and Review.

questions.stem: What defines the 'definite article' 'the'?

options.A: It is used when the specific identity of the noun is known to both the speaker and the listener.
options.B: It is only used before plural words.
options.C: It is only used before verbs.
options.D: It means the noun is totally unknown.

questions.explanation: Definite (the) is used when the noun is specific or its identity is already known to the listener.

questions.stem: __________ is used to introduce a list
questions.explanation: A colon is the punctuation mark used to introduce a list of items.

questions.stem: Which part of speech connects a dependent clause to an independent clause?
questions.explanation: Subordinating conjunctions connect a dependent clause to an independent clause.

questions.stem: Before you begin note-taking from a lecture, what is the first step you should take?

options.A: Start writing immediately to not miss anything.
options.B: Have a firm grasp of the message or topic being discussed.
options.C: Ask the lecturer to slow down.

questions.explanation: Before beginning note-taking, you must first have a firm grasp of the message or topic being discussed. This involves defining the purpose for listening.

questions.stem: How does a 'phrase' contrast with a 'clause'?

options.A: A phrase lacks a subject and predicate, whereas a clause contains both.
options.C: A phrase requires a question mark.

questions.explanation: A phrase is a group of words without a subject or a predicate; a clause contains a subject and a verb.

questions.stem: The URL of a website accredited to a post-secondary institution or institution of higher learning usually ends with.......
questions.explanation: Educational institutions typically use the .edu domain extension in their URLs.

questions.stem: What is the function of the 'headword' in a Noun Phrase?

options.B: It is the central noun that the modifiers and qualifiers describe.

questions.explanation: In an MHQ noun phrase, the Headword (H) is the core noun being modified.

questions.stem: The following are search techniques EXCEPT..............
questions.explanation: Filtering is not listed among the search techniques; Boolean, wild card, and truncation are.

questions.stem: What characterises a 'compound-complex sentence'?

options.C: It contains at least two main clauses and one or more subordinate clauses.

questions.explanation: A compound-complex sentence is a combination... it has two or more main clauses and one or more subordinate clauses.

questions.stem: After determining the basic idea of a paragraph, what is the second step in summarizing it?

options.C: Read it again to pick out the essentials.

questions.explanation: The second step is to read it again to pick out the essentials, summarizing mentally as you read.

questions.stem: In word formation, what is 'alphabetism'?

options.B: Forming a word from initials but pronouncing each letter individually, like 'FBI'.
options.C: Clipping the front of a word.

questions.explanation: Alphabetism involves forming a word from initial letters and pronouncing each letter individually (e.g., FUTA, FBI).

questions.stem: What should you try to discern about the writer during the first reading?

options.B: Their tone and what they are trying to achieve.

questions.explanation: During the first reading, you get insight into what the writer's tone suggests about their attitude and what they are trying to achieve (e.g., to persuade, inform).

questions.stem: Grammatical hierarchy in English is structured in which of the following ways?

options.A: morpheme, word, clause, phrase and sentence.
options.B: morpheme, word, phrase, clause and sentence.
options.C: sentence, phrase, clause, word and morpheme.
options.D: sentence, clause, phrase, word and sentence.

questions.explanation: The grammatical hierarchy from smallest to largest unit is: morpheme, word, phrase, clause, sentence.

questions.stem: When making notes from a textbook, what should you do after skimming the material?

options.C: Highlight or mark out the relevant part of the material.

questions.explanation: The strategy states: 'you must skim and highlight or mark out the relevant part of the material that contains the general or specific ideas of interest.'

questions.stem: Which of the following should not be capitalised?
questions.explanation: Chilean, Guatemalan (nationalities), and Gaelic (language) are proper adjectives and should be capitalized. 'Guesstimates' is a common noun and should not be capitalized.

questions.stem: Questions which require you to refer directly to the text are called
questions.explanation: Also known as literal questions, these require the reader to directly reference explicitly stated facts printed in the passage.

questions.stem: Fair use allows the usage of copyrighted works for ............
